stem: With the required determination in place, what is the micro-purchase threshold for a contingency buy made and performed outside the United States?

options.why: FAR 2.101 sets $40,000 outside the U.S. when the head of the agency makes the contingency or emergency determination.
$25,000 is the figure inside the United States.
$15,000 is the standard threshold without a determination.
That is the standard SAT.

stem: With the required determination, what is the simplified acquisition threshold for a contingency buy made and performed outside the United States?

options.why: FAR 2.101 sets $2 million outside the U.S. under a contingency or emergency determination.
$1 million is the figure inside the United States.
That is the standard SAT.
$15 million is the contingency ceiling for commercial simplified procedures.

stem: What is an SF 44?

options.text: A purchase order, invoice and voucher in one form, for small on-the-spot buys
options.why: The SF 44 is a common field tool for small immediate purchases.

options.text: A warrant certificate that a contingency contracting officer carries in the field
options.why: Warrants use the SF 1402.

options.text: A modification form for small purchase orders
options.why: Modifications use the SF 30.

options.text: A protest form for small business concerns
options.why: There is no standard protest form.

stem: Where do you check whether a contractor is excluded (suspended or debarred)?

options.why: Exclusions are recorded in SAM.
CPARS holds performance assessments.
WAWF handles invoices.
GFEBS is the Army's financial system.

stem: In DoW, COR appointments are made and tracked in:

options.why: JAM handles DoW appointments such as CORs.

options.text: SAM.gov, under the entity's points of contact
options.why: SAM is for vendors and notices.

options.text: AITAS, with the COR's training records

options.why: EDA holds signed DoW contracts and modifications for viewing.

options.text: Wide Area WorkFlow (WAWF) in PIEE, next to the invoices

options.text: The Joint Appointment Module (JAM) in PIEE

stem: Which exam area has the most questions on CON 3990V?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.why: Guiding Principles has 42 of the 150 questions; Contract Principles alone is 18 of them.
Award has 40 questions, the second most.
Post-Award has 38 questions, the third most.
Pre-Award has 30 questions, the fewest of the four areas.

stem: According to the exam FAQ, many questions stem from which FAR part?

options.why: The FAQ tells candidates to read Part 15 thoroughly.

options.text: Part 52, Solicitation Provisions and Contract Clauses

Part 1 matters, but the FAQ names Part 15.
Not named in the FAQ.

stem: What score passes CON 3990V?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.why: The exam is pass or fail at 70%.
75% is a good practice target, not the pass mark.
Higher than required.
Lower than required.

stem: With the contingency or emergency determination in place, what is the micro-purchase threshold for a buy made and performed inside the United States?

options.why: FAR 2.101 sets $25,000 inside the United States under a contingency or emergency determination ($40,000 outside).
That is the standard threshold with no determination.
That is the figure outside the United States.
That is the standard simplified acquisition threshold, not a micro-purchase figure.

stem: What is a field ordering officer (FOO)?
cite: Defense Contingency Contracting Handbook; unit standing procedures

options.text: A trained, appointed person who makes small purchases in the field within strict written limits, under a contracting officer
options.why: FOOs and paying agents extend the contracting office's reach in the field; they are not contracting officers and act only within their appointment.

options.text: A warranted contracting officer who deploys with the unit
options.why: That is a contingency contracting officer (CCO). A FOO holds no warrant.

options.text: The commander who approves requirements in theater
options.why: Requirements review boards and commanders approve requirements; they do not buy.

options.text: A contractor employee who delivers supplies to the forward operating base
options.why: A FOO is a Government person, usually a Soldier, not a contractor.

stem: A unit wants to use the higher contingency thresholds for an exercise buy. What must be in place first?

options.text: The head of the agency's determination that the buy supports a contingency operation or another listed situation
options.why: The higher thresholds apply only when the required determination covers that buy; without it, the standard figures apply.

options.text: A memorandum from the unit commander saying the buy is urgent and must be made this week
options.why: Urgency alone does not raise a threshold; it can justify an exception to competition, which is a different rule.

options.text: Nothing: units deployed outside the United States always use the higher thresholds
options.why: Being deployed does not by itself change the thresholds.

options.text: A class deviation signed by the contracting officer and filed with the purchase request
options.why: Contracting officers cannot issue deviations; the thresholds depend on the statutory determination.

stem: Which form is a purchase order, invoice and voucher in one, used for small over-the-counter buys delivered on the spot?

options.why: The SF 44 is the field tool for small immediate purchases where the supplies are delivered on the spot.
The SF 1449 is the commercial solicitation, contract and order form.
The SF 30 amends solicitations and modifies contracts.
The DD 1155 is DoW's order form for supplies or services, not a one-page purchase, invoice and voucher.

stem: Before award, what must you confirm in SAM.gov about the contractor?

options.text: That it is registered and is not listed as excluded (suspended or debarred)
options.why: Registration is required before award, and excluded contractors generally cannot receive new awards.

options.text: That it has posted its prices in Contract Opportunities
options.why: Contract Opportunities is where the Government posts notices, not where vendors post prices.

options.text: That it holds a GSA Schedule contract
options.why: A schedule contract is one way to buy, not a condition of award.

options.text: That its CPARS ratings are all Exceptional
options.why: Past performance is evaluated where the solicitation says so; perfect ratings are not a condition of award.

stem: Which system is the Army's contract writing system, the one a specialist uses to release solicitations and awards?

options.text: ACWS, the Army Contract Writing System
options.why: ACWS replaced the older PD2 and SPS systems; without a role in it you cannot release actions.
GFEBS is the Army's financial system, where purchase requests and funds live.
The Virtual Contracting Enterprise holds contract files and the warrant process, not the writing of solicitations.
CPARS records contractor performance after award.

stem: Why should a new 51C ask for system roles in the first week on the job?
cite: Lesson 34; the owner's experience in contracting support brigades

options.text: A role can take two to three weeks to approve, and you cannot work actions without it
options.why: Approval depends on how fast you request the role and how fast the local system administrators act; waiting to ask delays your first action.

options.text: Roles expire if they are not requested in the first five days
options.why: There is no such rule; the point is the approval time.

options.text: Only new Soldiers may hold system roles
options.why: Roles follow the job, not the date of arrival.

options.text: Your supervisor cannot assign work until you have CPARS access
options.why: CPARS is one system among several; the contract writing system matters more for day-to-day actions.

stem: How many attempts at CON 3990V do you get, and how far apart?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.text: Three attempts in 12 months, at least 30 days apart
options.why: Counted from your first try. A fourth attempt is possible one year after the first failed try.
Attempts are limited and spaced.
The rule is three in 12 months, not two for life.
The window is 12 months from the first try, with up to three attempts.

stem: What may you bring into the CON 3990V exam room to look things up?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.text: Nothing: the exam is closed book, with no FAR, notes, phone or computer
options.why: Everything goes in a locker; you answer from memory, which is why the part titles and key numbers must be automatic.

options.text: A printed copy of the FAR, with your own tabs and highlights
options.why: No references are allowed.

options.text: One page of handwritten notes on the key numbers and part titles
options.why: No notes are allowed.

options.text: Your phone in airplane mode, for the calculator only
options.why: Phones and smartwatches go in a locker.

stem: You did not pass your first attempt at CON 3990V. What does DoW require before your next try?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.text: CON 3900V, the instructor-led exam preparation course (CON 3910 is its prerequisite)
options.why: After a first failed attempt, CON 3900V is required before the next try, unless you already took it. Then wait at least 30 days and apply again in AITAS.

options.text: Retaking CON 1100V through CON 1400V before you may test again
options.why: The certification courses are not repeated after a failed exam.

options.text: A written exception to policy from the DACM before a second attempt
options.why: No exception is needed for a second or third attempt inside the 12-month window.

options.text: Nothing: you may retest the next day if a seat is available
options.why: Attempts must be at least 30 days apart, and CON 3900V comes first.

stem: About how much time do you have per question on CON 3990V?
cite: DoW Contracting Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

options.why: Three hours of seat time for 150 questions, including the tutorial and your review, works out to about 72 seconds each. Flag hard ones and come back.
That would be 150 questions in 75 minutes.
That would need 5 hours.
The exam is timed: 3 hours.
